explanation: Argon makes up almost 1% of dry air, many times more than carbon dioxide. Most of it came from the slow radioactive decay of potassium in rocks.

claims.text: After nitrogen and oxygen, argon is the most abundant gas in dry air.
Carbon dioxide (about 0.04%), hydrogen and helium each make up far less of dry air than argon does.
Argon makes up almost 1% (about 0.93%) of dry air.
Dry air holds many times more argon than carbon dioxide.
Most of the argon in Earth's atmosphere is argon-40, produced by the radioactive decay of potassium-40 in rocks.
